audit.summary: The aero subsystem maps a WingSpec onto an AeroSandbox (ASB) Airplane and runs a small envelope of operating points to extract totals (L/D/side, moments, CL/CD/Cm, q) and per-panel spanwise loads, scaled by a per-case safety/gust factor, then hands a spanwise normal-force density q(y) to structural sizing. It is built around a horizontal free-flying cantilever wing abstraction (lift = heel force) and a tiny 5 m demo dinghy load envelope. For the Oyster-595 twin-mast NACA-0018 wingsail re-scope, the geometric mapping and per-panel KJ extraction (model.py, loads.py mechanics) are largely reusable, but the load-case envelope (cases.py), the single-wing/no-mast/no-tandem aero model, and the absent hurricane-survival + weathervane-drag physics are the core gaps. Verdict: keep loads.py plumbing, refactor model.py and scenario wiring, retire/rewrite cases.py and the example's hand-rolled root-moment math.

modules.purpose: Defines LoadCase (frozen dataclass: name, airspeed_mps=AWS, alpha_deg=trim AoA, altitude_m, safety_factor, description) and DESIGN_CASES, a 5-case envelope tuned for a 5 m demo dinghy wingsail.
key_apis: LoadCase(name, airspeed_mps, alpha_deg, altitude_m=0, safety_factor=1.0, description='')
modules.notes: The LoadCase schema itself is fine and could survive a refactor, but the DESIGN_CASES values are dinghy-scale and physically wrong for an Oyster-595 free-standing wingmast: max AWS is 25 m/s (~49 kt) which is nowhere near hurricane survival (64+ kt = 33+ m/s, design gust to ~55-70 m/s). No feathered/weathervaned hurricane case at storm wind. safety_factor is overloaded as a gust factor (only 1.5 once). No heel/pitch attitude, no air-density-at-sea-level vs altitude (altitude_m always 0 for a boat). Survival case assumes AoA can be 'dumped' to 6 deg, but a free-rotating mast weathervanes to ~0 and must survive at the resulting residual/buffet loads. Needs a full sailboat-specific rewrite.

modules.purpose: Runs ASB solvers and packages results. run_case uses AeroBuildup (fast totals); run_case_lifting_line uses LiftingLine and attaches PanelLoads (per-panel KJ force vectors). AeroResult carries totals + safety-factored spanwise normal-force density q(y) via distributed_normal_force (LL panel interp, elliptic fallback). sweep_envelope iterates cases.
key_apis: PanelLoads(centers_xyz, areas, forces_xyz, normals_xyz, chords, spanwise_widths)
modules.notes: Mechanically solid and the right interface for structural sizing. KJ panel extraction F = rho*Gamma*(V_inf x dl_bound) is correct. Reusable as-is for a single mast. Gaps for the new spec: (1) only +Z 'lift' is fed to the beam (drag/side/tangential traction and the pivot/pitching moment that twists a free-rotating mast are computed but not distributed spanwise); (2) elliptic fallback assumes an untwisted free wing — a deck-rooted mast has a wall/ground-plane image and tip vortex that change the loading; (3) no tandem/twin-mast interaction. Refactor to also expose distributed chordwise/tangential and torsional loads, but the module skeleton stays.

modules.purpose: Builds an ASB Wing/Airplane from a WingSpec: one WingXSec per taper knot, NACA00xx airfoil, computes mean aero chord by trapezoidal area integration, sets s_ref/b_ref/c_ref. Models the wingsail as a horizontal cantilever (ASB convention chord +X, span +Y, normal +Z); structural span +Z maps to ASB +Y.
modules.notes: Geometry mapping is reusable and NACA-0018 (thickness=0.18) is already the family default, matching the new spec exactly. But the abstraction is a single free-flying symmetric=False wing with no ground/deck plane, no mast/spar aero, and no second sail. For a deck-rooted free-standing mast it needs: a symmetry/image plane at the root (sea surface) so the root sees ~2x effective AR (or explicit wall BC); a twin-mast Airplane (two Wings) to capture tandem slot/downwash interaction; and ideally the rotating spar fairing exposed to flow for weathervane-drag. AoA here is geometric trim relative to apparent wind, which still maps, but heel angle is unmodeled.

modules.purpose: Central DesignParameters container (geometry, material, iso-equivalent knockdowns, load_cases, mesh, aero solver knobs, frame-field, skin) with small/medium/large_scenario builders. AeroParameters holds only spanwise_resolution (STANDARD_AERO=16). Wires DESIGN_CASES into load_cases.
key_apis: DesignParameters(geometry, material, material_iso, load_cases, mesh, aero, frame_field, skin_sizing)
modules.notes: Self-described as scoped to Phase 4-5 only (FEA + frame field), no sizing/topology params. The umbrella pattern is worth keeping, but for the wingmast re-scope it needs: sailboat platform params (deck height, mast spacing/tandem geometry, design heel, sea-level density), an explicit hurricane-survival case set, and the new minimum-mass sizing objective hookup. The three demo scenarios (5/22/45 m free wingsails) are not Oyster-595 wingmasts and should be re-derived to the boat's righting-moment / sail-area envelope.

modules.purpose: Measurement-record script: sweeps DESIGN_CASES over LiftingLine for medium_wingsail, prints per-case CL/CD/factored-L/D and a hand-computed root bending moment M_root = L_factored * 4b/(3*pi) (half-ellipse centroid), identifies the governing case, and dumps the spanwise q(y) profile.
modules.notes: Good template for an aero-envelope report, but its physics are demo-grade: the root-moment formula assumes a pure elliptic free-wing load and a horizontal cantilever, ignores deck-plane image, drag/torsion, and self/structural weight, and uses the dinghy DESIGN_CASES. Reuse the report structure; replace the envelope and the closed-form moment with the actual distributed load integrated against the mast structural model. Note default sweep_envelope method is 'buildup' (totals only) — the example passes no method so it does NOT get per-panel data despite the docstring saying LiftingLine.

durable_knowledge: Demo wingsail aero envelope (DESIGN_CASES, 5 m dinghy scale): nominal_trim AWS=10 m/s AoA=8 deg (near best L/D); max_aoa AWS=15 AoA=12 (approaching stall); design_gust AWS=15 AoA=8 with safety_factor=1.5; survival AWS=25 AoA=6 (dumped AoA); feathered AWS=25 AoA=0. safety_factor is the only gust/dynamic-load multiplier and defaults to 1.0.

Gust/dynamic factor model is a single scalar per case (LoadCase.safety_factor), applied multiplicatively to lift and spanwise q(y) via AeroResult.factored_normal_force_N and distributed_normal_force. Only the design_gust case uses 1.5; this is the project's entire current dynamic-amplification model.

Per-panel aero load uses Kutta-Joukowski: F_panel = rho * Gamma * (V_inf x dl_bound), applied at the panel centroid (mean of 4 LL vertices); spanwise width approximated as |bound_leg_y|. This is the load-distribution physics fed to structural sizing.

Spanwise lift distribution fallback (no LL panels) is analytic elliptic: q(y) = (4L/(pi*b)) * sqrt(1 - (y/b)^2), and the half-ellipse load centroid gives root bending M_root = L * 4b/(3*pi) (used in example 02).
Dynamic pressure recorded per case as q = 0.5 * rho * V^2 with rho from asb.Atmosphere(altitude_m); altitude is always 0 for the boat use-case so rho ~= 1.225 kg/m^3.

Airfoil family is NACA-00xx, default thickness t/c = 0.18 (NACA-0018) across all three demo sizes — already matches the new wingmast spec. Pivot/rotation axis at 25% chord (pivot_frac=0.25) at every station.
Spar radius rule: largest circle inscribed in the root airfoil centered at the pivot, floored to the nearest cm (~0.08 m for NACA-0018, 1 m chord, 25% pivot).
Demo wing family aspect ratio ~6.1-6.25 (span / mean chord); taper ~0.6 (tip/root). Free-flying cantilever, symmetric=False, no ground/deck image plane.

Two ASB solvers wired: AeroBuildup (fast, totals only, default in sweep_envelope) and LiftingLine (slower, per-panel forces, default spanwise_resolution=12; scenario STANDARD_AERO uses 16). Project convention (CLAUDE.md) is to measure wall-clock for every run.
gaps_for_new_spec: Hurricane-survival aerodynamic loads: current max AWS is 25 m/s (~49 kt). Need a genuine storm/survival envelope (sustained 64+ kt = 33+ m/s, gusts to ~55-70 m/s) with the free-rotating mast weathervaned. Define survival q and the residual loads on a feathered (AoA~0) NACA-0018 plus the fairing/spar bluff-body drag.

Free-rotating-mast weathervane drag: at feather the dominant load is profile + bluff-body drag on the airfoil and the exposed cylindrical spar fairing, not lift. AeroBuildup/LiftingLine do not capture separated bluff-body drag of the rotating spar; need a drag-area (Cd*A) model for the spar/fairing and stalled-section drag for the survival case.

Twin-mast / tandem slot effect: two NACA-0018 wingsails in tandem on the Oyster-595 interact (slot acceleration, downwash, fore/aft mast loading split). Current model is a single isolated wing; need a 2-wing ASB Airplane or a tandem-interaction correction, and per-mast load partition for sizing each mast.

Deck/sea-surface ground-plane image: a deck-rooted vertical mast has an image plane at the root (effective AR ~2x, root loading altered). Current model is a free cantilever with elliptic-style tip-to-tip loading; needs a symmetry plane or wall BC at z=0.

Sailboat load-attitude coupling: heel angle, apparent-wind triangle (boat speed + true wind -> AWS/AWA), and the boat righting-moment limit that actually caps usable sail force. None modeled; LoadCase has only AWS + geometric AoA.

Distributed non-normal loads for sizing: only +Z (normal/lift) is distributed spanwise. The free-rotating mast is governed by the pitching moment about the 25% pivot (drives torsion/twist and the rotation bearing) plus drag; loads.py computes total pitch/yaw/roll moments and drag but does not distribute drag/torsion along the span for the structural model.

Operational vs survival objective split: minimum-mass sizing under BOTH operational (performance) and hurricane (survival) load sets requires a clear case classification + load/resistance factors per case; current safety_factor scalar conflates gust and material safety and is set ad hoc.

Vortex-induced / dynamic response of the slender free-standing mast (vortex shedding, lock-in, gust dynamic amplification) is unmodeled; the single 1.5 gust factor is unlikely to be adequate for a 30-50 m free-standing storm-loaded mast.

audit.summary: The active sizing path is laminate_sizing.py (orchestrator) + sensitivity.py (analytic adjoint Jacobian + KS engine), built on a generic named-block design vector (design_vector.py) and named constraint specs (constraints.py). It co-sizes a "form-beam + load-bearing skin" topology: longitudinal beams (circular or annular/hollow) following the OML, tiled into a triangulated CLT-laminate shell, with optional core tube, sandwich skin, and lateral bracing rings. The geometry generator (shell_model.py + splines/cross_section/sections/build) is hardwired to ONE topology: n_beams discrete beam lines arc-spaced around the airfoil OML at n_levels spanwise stations, with the skin = quad-strips-between-adjacent-beams split into 2 triangles each. This is structurally MISALIGNED with the new wingmast concept (3+ filament-wound hollow BOX spars + UD longerons filling inter-spar channels + outer wound shell): there is no box-spar primitive (only circular/annular round sections), no inter-spar channel/longeron concept, no co-bond/co-cure interface modeling, and no rotating-stock/journal/bearing boundary condition. The NLP machinery (adjoint engine, KS aggregation, multistart, warm-start, shadow prices, FD-validated gradients, IPOPT/SLSQP backends, stock-catalog CP-SAT) is high-quality, well-tested, topology-agnostic infrastructure that should be KEPT and reused; the geometry/cross-section/model-build layer must be REFACTORED or rebuilt for the box-spar + longeron + shell parametrization. The codebase is the product of a long FEA-in-the-loop optimization campaign (small 25.13 kg / medium ~1021.6 kg foundation-buckling-governed headlines); the conventions (ulp-discipline bit-reproducibility, incumbent guard, KS soft-max for large migrations, n_workers=1 RAM cap, eigen-verify at n>=24) are durable lessons.

modules.purpose: Active sizing orchestrator. size_beam_shell_laminate co-sizes [r_group(G), t_band(B), f0(L), f45(L) | optional r_tube(S), t_wall(S) | t_hollow(H) | t_core(B) | brace_radius(1)] minimizing normalized mass under beam von-Mises, skin vM/Tsai-Wu, tip deflection, tip twist, beam-Euler/foundation buckling, panel buckling, tube-wall buckling, core wrinkle/crimp, layup-simplex, monotonic-taper, and annulus-validity constraints. Builds CLT laminate from layup fractions, solves combined beam+shell FEA per (aero x accel) load combo, runs SLSQP or IPOPT, returns LaminateSizingResult.
key_apis: size_beam_shell_laminate(model, load_arrays, config, *, ply, rho, maxiter, ftol, x0, panel_pressures) -> LaminateSizingResult

LaminateSizingConfig (frozen dataclass: sigma_allow_Pa, tip limits, r/t bounds, buckling_safety_factor, ks_rho, beam_buckling_model, panel_d_mode, ply_angle_datum, optimizer, core, accel_vectors, use_analytic_jacobian)
modules.notes: 1786 lines, the orchestration heart. Constraint formulation (all g>=0 feasible, normalized by limit), incumbent guard (keeps lightest hard-feasible iterate; converged=False if endpoint beaten), per-band layup, datum-frame ply angles, V.4 design-dependent body loads with adjoint dF/dx, are all topology-agnostic and worth keeping. What must change for the box-spar concept: build_sections only emits BeamSection.circular/annular (no box section); the design vector blocks assume round-beam radii + a single uniform skin laminate; there is no longeron/channel block, no co-bond/co-cure interface DV, no journal/bearing BC. The orchestration pattern (DesignVector blocks + ConstraintSpec list + jac registration + shadow-price attribution) is the right scaffold to extend, hence refactor not retire.

modules.purpose: Analytic adjoint Jacobian primitives + KS aggregation engine. Element-stiffness derivatives (dkloc_dr, dkloc_annular, dAD_dt[_sandwich], dD_dc_sandwich, dQeff_df) exploit linearity of the FEA element routines in section/laminate inputs. Adjoint engine (adjoint_lambda, prepare_sensitivity/SensCache, lambdaT_dK_x_cached) contracts lambda^T (dK/dx) u once per design point, reused across all constraints/load cases. Per-constraint gradients (grad_beam_vm, grad_skin_vm, grad_panel_buckling, grad_beam_buckling, grad_tube_wall_one, grad_core_check, grad_skin_tsai_wu, grad_tip_defl, grad_tip_twist) and KS providers (provider_panel/beam_buck/defl/twist/skin_vm/core_check/tube_wall) feeding grad_ks_engine.
key_apis: DesignSens (dataclass: model, G, B, L, group_of_element, band_of_tri, radii_full, Qeff_tri, offset_tri, tube/hollow/core/foundation/brace fields)
grad_ks_engine(facs, ds, cache, dFs, rho, provider) -> (con, grad)
modules.notes: 1490 lines. The adjoint + KS machinery is mathematically general (lambda^T dK/dx u over any element DV), but every gradient and provider is written against round-beam (circular/annular) section formulas (sigma_n = |N|/A + M r/I, A=pi r^2, etc.) and the triangle-CLT shell. A box-spar/longeron parametrization needs NEW element-derivative primitives (box-section dA/dt_wall, dI/dwidth, channel-fill longeron area) and NEW providers, but the adjoint contraction, KS aggregation, SensCache caching, and the design-only dK/dx assembly pattern transfer directly. Every analytic gradient is FD-validated in tests/beams/test_sensitivity.py — same discipline required for any new primitive.

modules.purpose: Builds the BeamShellModel: arc-spaced beam grid (n_beams lines x n_levels stations) along the OML, longitudinal beam elements, a triangulated load-bearing skin (each adjacent-beam quad split into 2 triangles), fixed keel ring, tip ring. Optional core tube on the pivot axis, hollow form beams, lateral-bracing rings. Provides skin_panel_widths (strip buckling b), skin_datum_angles (global ply datum), beam_adjacent_widths (foundation k geometry), braced_segment_mask.

BeamShellModel (frozen dataclass: nodes, beam_elements, shell_tris, n_beams, n_levels, fixed_nodes, tip_nodes, E/G_beam, tube/hollow/brace fields, n_form_elements property)
modules.notes: This is the topology lock-in. The model hardcodes: round beams as discrete OML-following lines, skin as beam-to-beam triangle strips, radius-symmetry grouping, keel-clamped cantilever BC. The new concept (3+ box spars + inter-spar longeron channels + outer wound shell) has a fundamentally different cross-section topology — box-spar webs/caps, longeron-filled channels between spars, and a free-rotating wingmast needs a journal/bearing root BC not a fixed keel ring. Needs a new model builder; some helpers (datum angles, panel widths, foundation geometry) generalize.

These compute the radius-group / skin-band layout the whole active path depends on.

These helpers are tightly coupled to the round-beam + triangle-strip topology (beam_radius_groups assumes chord-mirrored beam lines; skin_band_map tiles 2 tris per (level,beam)). They should be extracted/refactored into a non-frozen geometry module and re-derived for the box-spar topology.

Directly relevant to the new 'rotating stock / journals' requirement: the same CP-SAT pattern can discretize spar wall thickness / longeron count / wound-tow stock. durable_knowledge: DESIGN VECTOR LAYOUT (active path): x = [r_group(G), t_band(B), f0(L), f45(L)] with optional appended blocks in order [r_tube(S), t_wall(S)], [t_hollow(H)], [t_core(B)], [brace_radius(1)]. nx = G+B+2L+extras. G = radius groups (chord-mirror symmetric beams SHARE radii via beam_radius_groups; falls back to one-per-element if asymmetric). B = spanwise skin thickness bands. L = layup groups (=B if per_band_layup else 1). f90 = 1 - f0 - f45 eliminated. Blocks declared via DesignVector named-block abstraction.

CONSTRAINT FORMULATION: every constraint is an inequality g(x) >= 0 (feasible), each normalized O(1) by its limit. limit-type g = 1 - v/L; safety-factor g = 1 - SF*v/cap (or R/SF - 1 for Tsai-Wu). Constraints: beam_vm (per element, n rows), skin (vM or Tsai-Wu), defl, twist, beam_buck, panel_buck, tube_wall, core_wrinkle, core_crimp, frac (layup simplex f0+f45<=1), mono (monotonic radius taper keel->tip), hollow/tube validity (r-t>=0), tube_mono. Each is one ConstraintSpec append; jac registered by name; shadow-price attribution structural.

KS AGGREGATION (V.0.3/P#7): when config.ks_rho set (e.g. 50.0), each max-based constraint family becomes ONE smooth KS scalar over (items x load combos), removing argmax Jacobian kinks that stall optimizers on large design migrations. ks_aggregate(vals,rho) = max + log(sum exp(rho*(v-max)))/rho, returns numerically-stable softmax weights. Conservative (KS >= max). Requires use_analytic_jacobian. Hard maxes still drive feasibility/reporting. KS+IPOPT closed the P.3 sandwich migration (1679.3 kg) that 6 hard-max attempts could not.

ADJOINT ENGINE: prepare_sensitivity builds design-only dK/dx element matrices ONCE per design point (SensCache), reused across every load case and constraint gradient. Per constraint: solve K lambda = dg/du (adjoint_lambda), then grad contribution = -lambda^T (dK/dx) u (lambdaT_dK_x_cached) plus explicit section-property terms plus lambda^T dF/dx for design-dependent body loads (V.4). Element derivatives exploit FEA-routine linearity in (A,Iy,Iz,J) and laminate (A,D). Every analytic gradient FD-validated (central diff, rel-err <= ~1e-4) in tests/beams/test_sensitivity.py.

MULTISTART (V.0.4): size_beam_shell_laminate_multistart runs n_starts guesses; start 0 = default or x0, starts 1.. = seeded-RNG uniform within bounds (simplex-projected). n_workers>1 fans over ProcessPoolExecutor (identical to serial; starts independent). macOS spawn requires __main__ guard. Selection: min-mass among hard-feasible (laminate_result_is_feasible), else min-mass overall with n_feasible=0.

WARM-START CONVENTIONS: sweeps/refinements seed from nearest prior optimum via x0=, built by design_vector_from_result. Absent blocks padded EQUIVALENCE-PRESERVING (t_hollow seeds at group radius -> clamps solid; t_core at 0 -> exactly monolithic) so the seed evaluates identically to the prior optimum (hard-feasible -> incumbent-guarded -> can never produce a worse result). A 3mm t_hollow pad once lost a stage (infeasible seed, no convergence in 500 iters). Fine meshes resample coarse solutions (resample_segment_radii).

INCUMBENT GUARD: evaluate() tracks the lightest HARD-feasible iterate visited (mass within 1e-3 tol on all active constraints). If the optimizer endpoint is heavier or infeasible, the incumbent is returned with used_incumbent=True and converged=False (it is a feasible design, not a certified optimum).

IPOPT vs SLSQP: SLSQP (scipy) default; IPOPT (cyipopt minimize_ipopt, limited-memory Hessian, adaptive mu) is the documented fallback when SLSQP active-set stalls (trigger: DVs > ~150 or persistent stalls, e.g. sandwich skin->core migration). IPOPT warm-start requires warm_start_init_point=yes + mu_init=1e-6 + tiny bound_push, else the barrier init centers the iterate (=cold start). Shadow prices are SLSQP-only (IPOPT multiplier signs unwired).

BUCKLING VERIFICATION: judge feasibility on a CONVERGED mesh (n_levels >= 24), not the 16x8 sizing mesh. The n=8 linear-buckling eigen is unconservatively overstiff (overshoots low at n~12, settles to a cluster floor by n>=24). Closed-form foundation buckling (Pcr = 2 sqrt(k EI), k = 3 D22_chord (1/w_l^3 + 1/w_r^3) from adjacent skin strips) is well-calibrated to the converged eigen for the OPERATIONAL envelope but NON-conservative for slam — slam-sized designs must be eigen-verified at n>=24.

MEMORY/RUN DISCIPLINE: an IPOPT medium-16x8 worker peaks ~18 GiB; on a 32 GiB machine safe cap is n_workers=1 (two coincident peaks ~36 GiB). 8-way multistart oversubscribed RAM and caused two watchdog kernel panics. Always MEASURE wall-clock (estimates run ~10x off). Record ru_maxrss.

ULP DISCIPLINE: several code paths deliberately keep character-identical float expressions (e.g. panel_width_mode sqrt-roundtrip, no-tube body-load product association) because 1-ulp changes shift SLSQP cold-start basins on small problems and break bit-reproducibility of recorded headlines.

HEADLINE MASSES (campaign record): small (5m) 25.13 kg (4-band, lambda_cr 2.00), medium (22m) ~1021.6 kg foundation-design eigen-verified; beam buckling is the SOLE binding lever on the 1021.6 kg optimum (buckling_sf_beam = +1030.8 kg/SF, every other shadow price 0). 16 beams measured optimal. Tube + hollow form beams = 1924.6 kg (lambda 2.54). Scales 1m drone wing -> 100m turbine blade.

PLY-ANGLE DATUM (E.4b): default ply angles are measured per-triangle-local-frame (NOT a globally consistent layup). Set config.ply_angle_datum (e.g. (0,0,1)=span) to measure against a global datum via skin_datum_angles + laminate_stiffness_offset, making the optimized layup a manufacturable global prescription (0deg = datum). Required by the foundation buckling model and datum_ortho panel buckling (need a coherent chord direction).
gaps_for_new_spec: BOX-SPAR PARAMETRIZATION: there is no box (hollow rectangular/airfoil-conforming) cross-section primitive anywhere. BeamSection supports only .circular and .annular (round). The new concept needs a filament-wound hollow box spar: web height, cap width, wall thickness(es), and the FEA element-stiffness + dA/dt, dI/dwidth analytic derivatives, plus a CAD loft builder. All current section math (vM sigma_n=|N|/A + M r/I with A=pi r^2, panel D11 from triangle CLT) assumes round beams / triangle skin.

MULTI-SPAR TOPOLOGY: build_beam_shell_model hardcodes one topology — n_beams discrete lines arc-spaced around the OML perimeter, skin = beam-to-beam triangle strips. The new concept is 3+ box spars at chordwise stations co-bonded into the airfoil. Needs a new model builder placing spar boxes at interior chordwise positions, the inter-spar regions as distinct entities, and beam_radius_groups / skin_band_map re-derived (they assume chord-mirrored perimeter beam lines).

LONGERON CHANNEL FILLING: no concept of UD longerons filling inter-spar channels exists. Needs DV blocks for longeron cross-section/count per channel, the channel-geometry definition (bounded by adjacent spar walls + inner/outer shell), longeron mass/stiffness contribution to the FEA, and analytic gradients. The DesignVector named-block scaffold supports adding these blocks cleanly.

CO-BOND vs CO-CURE INTERFACES: no interface/bondline modeling. The current 'massless stiff bond' mechanism (gusset_elements: assembled into K, excluded from mass/recovery — used for tube->beam bonds) is the closest existing primitive, but there is no model of co-bond vs co-cure stiffness, bondline shear allowables, or a manufacturability constraint distinguishing the two. Needs interface-stiffness DOFs and a bondline strength constraint spec.

ROTATING STOCK / JOURNALS / BEARINGS: the model uses a FIXED keel-ring clamp (fixed_nodes at the keel level) — a cantilever BC. A free-rotating wingmast needs a journal/bearing root boundary condition (radial reaction, free rotation about the mast axis, axial/thrust bearing), not a clamp. No bearing BC, no journal/trunnion geometry, no rotating-stock catalog (stock_catalog.py discretizes round radii only). The free-rotating-wing divergence/flutter check (V#6) is also absent.

BOX-SPAR PANEL/LOCAL BUCKLING: panel_buckling_utilization and the foundation beam-buckling model are written for triangle skin panels and round form-beams-on-skin-foundation. Box-spar webs and caps have their own local buckling modes (web shear buckling, cap compression buckling) that have no representation. New buckling constraints + KS providers + FD-validated gradients required.

FILAMENT-WINDING MANUFACTURABILITY: hollow_beams enforces a straightness/windability tol, but there is no model of wound fiber-angle limits on a box (geodesic/non-geodesic winding feasibility on a rectangular mandrel), tow-bandwidth, or wound vs RTM fiber knockdown for the box spars and outer shell. The as-wound orientation map / wound Vf model is noted as deferred (Phase G).

AERO LOAD PROJECTION ONTO NEW MESH: project_panels_to_skin / panel_pressure_per_tri assign aero panel forces to shell_tris (the beam-to-beam triangle skin). With a box-spar + outer-shell mesh the load-bearing surface changes; the projection target and the pressure->strip-bending check must be retargeted.

MASS/SELF-WEIGHT FOR NEW SECTIONS: body_load_vector/body_load_jacobian compute beam mass as pi r^2 (or annular) and triangle skin mass; box-spar walls, longeron fills, and the wound outer shell each need their own mass + dF/dx terms for the self-weight/inertial (heel/slam) load cases — important at the 100m turbine-blade scale.

SHADOW PRICES UNDER IPOPT: shadow_prices_from_specs is SLSQP-only; for the larger box-spar+longeron design vector (likely >150 DVs -> IPOPT regime) the KKT multiplier extraction/sign convention for IPOPT must be wired to keep the shadow-price lever analysis (which drives the whole optimization-progress methodology).

audit.summary:
A small, self-contained, dependency-light (numpy + scipy.sparse) linear FEM stack for the wingsail. Three independent element families: (1) volumetric linear (constant-strain) tetrahedra in fea.py — the original Phase-4 spike, isotropic only; (2) the live path: a 6-DOF/node flat-shell triangle (CST membrane + DKT bending + drilling penalty) in shell.py that accepts full CLT A/D laminate matrices, combined with 3D Euler-Bernoulli beams (frame.py) in beam_shell.py to model the form-beam + load-bearing-skin structure; (3) a linear eigen-buckling path (geometric_stiffness.py builds Kσ from the solved stress state, eigen_buckling.py solves K φ = −λ Kσ φ via dense Cholesky reduction). buckling.py holds closed-form utilization checks (Euler column, cylinder wall-crimp, SS-plate panel, elastic-foundation stringer) used as in-loop sizing constraints; the eigen path is the verification check. mesh.py tet-meshes the OML through gmsh; projection.py maps aero panel loads to OML tris; shell.py also tet-derives a surface ShellMesh. beam.py is a frozen legacy AeroSandbox tube-spar sizer.

The shell+beam+buckling triplet is the keeper and is directly reusable for a cantilever spar: it already does bending/twist/deflection (6-DOF nodes), composite shell mechanics via CLT, geometric anisotropy mapping (per-element offset-datum laminate → full 3x3 A/D with A16/A26), and the linear-eigen + closed-form buckling pair CLAUDE.md describes. The dominant gap for the re-scope is the boundary condition: the entire stack only supports full 6-DOF Dirichlet clamps (u=0). The rotating base in journal bearings (heel-step + deck-partners) — which restrains translation/some rotation but RELEASES the pitch-axis rotation (free-rotating) and provides two spanwise-separated radial supports rather than one root clamp — has no representation. No co-bond/co-cure interface elements, no contact, no filament-wound helical-angle → ply-angle mapping (CLT takes 0/±45/90 area fractions, not a wind angle field).

modules.purpose: Volumetric linear-elastic FEA on linear (constant-strain) tetrahedra; Phase-4 spike. K_e = V·BᵀDB, sparse LU solve, per-tet + Loubignac (volume-weighted) nodal stress recovery, von Mises. Isotropic-equivalent CFRP (single quasi-iso E,ν) or per-tet E.
modules.notes: Element type: 4-node linear tet (CST-equivalent, 1 Gauss pt, 3 DOF/node = no rotations). Isotropic only — D is the 6x6 isotropic Voigt matrix; no anisotropic/laminate path here. BC: full clamp on dirichlet_nodes. Reference/comparison implementation; NOT on the live laminate sizing path. For a thin-walled wingmast spar a shell model is far more efficient than 3D tets, and this module gives no composite layup or buckling. Keep only if a volumetric stress-line/detail check is wanted, otherwise retire.

modules.purpose: Flat-shell triangle FEA — the architectural core. 18-DOF triangle: CST membrane + DKT bending (Batoz-Bathe-Ho 1980) + drilling-θz penalty, rotated to global. Isotropic _element_K and the laminate tri_element_stiffness_laminate(A,D) that takes CLT membrane A (3x3 N/m) and bending D (3x3 N·m). Membrane/strain/stress recovery in element-local frame, principal directions for stress-line tracing.
modules.notes: Element: 3-node flat triangle, 6 DOF/node (u,v,w,θx,θy,θz). Drilling stiffness is a NON-physical penalty (default drilling_factor=1e-4 of G·t·A or A66) — needed only for positive-definiteness of non-coplanar assemblies; a single flat panel with this penalty is artificially soft in θz. Laminate path reduces EXACTLY to isotropic when A=t·Dm, D=(t³/12)·Dm (test_laminate_element). Accepts the full 3x3 anisotropic A/D including A16/A26 coupling (this is the composite-shell capability to keep). Flat-faceted shell — curvature captured only by faceting, no shear-deformable (Mindlin) option, no transverse-shear/ILSS. solve_shell_elastic clamps all 6 DOF on dirichlet_nodes.

modules.purpose: Phase-3 tapered tube-spar sizer built on AeroSandbox TubeSparBendingStructure: minimize spar mass s.t. axial stress, Euler column buckling, tip deflection, airfoil-envelope fit. Linearly-tapered 4-var (D_root,D_tip,t_root,t_tip).
modules.notes: Legacy/frozen baseline (CLAUDE.md: 'Legacy sizers are frozen'). Isotropic-equivalent only; depends on aerosandbox + geometry.wing WingSpec + aero.loads.AeroResult, all of which the re-scope changes. Conceptually closest to the new cantilever-spar problem (it IS a cantilever tube-spar sizer) so worth reading as a reference, but the implementation should not be reused as-is. Retire/rewrite against the new spec.

modules.purpose: Combined beam + shell assembler — the live FEA backend. Assembles 3D Euler-Bernoulli beams (frame.local_beam_stiffness) and DKT+CST shell tris into one 6-DOF global K, applies clamp BCs, solves, recovers per-beam axial/bending/torsion. Has isotropic (solve_beam_shell) and CLT-laminate (solve_beam_shell_laminate) variants; the *_factored variant returns the splu LU factorization for reuse in adjoint sensitivity solves.
key_apis: _assemble_beam_shell_laminate(...) (shared assembler, supports per-triangle A/D and optional gusset elements)
modules.notes: A_skin/D_skin may be (3,3) uniform or (M,3,3) per-triangle — this is where filament-wound spatially-varying anisotropy WOULD enter (per-tri Qbar from a wind-angle field). loads is (N,6). BC: fixed_nodes are fully clamped (all 6 DOF) — the single biggest re-scope gap (rotating journal base needs partial/released DOFs at two spanwise stations, not one full clamp). Beam-force recovery (bending = max sqrt(My²+Mz²) over the two ends) is only a valid stress proxy for Iy==Iz (circular). Assembly uses python triple-loops over elements (rows/cols/vals lists) — fine at sizing-mesh scale (~16x8, ~800 free DOF) but not for fine meshes.

modules.purpose: Closed-form per-element buckling UTILIZATION checks (demand·SF/capacity, feasible when ≤1) used as in-loop sizing constraints: Euler column (radius or explicit I), cylinder wall-crimping (NASA SP-8007 knockdown 0.65, σcr=knockdown·0.605·E·t/r), SS flat-plate panel (kc=4, σcr=kc·π²·D11/(b²t)), and elastic-foundation stringer (Pcr=2√(k·EI)). Plus k_ring_stiffness for smeared ring foundation.
modules.notes: These are the cheap analytic constraints; the eigen path is the verification. Documented caveats: panel default b=sqrt(area) mis-scales (backlog V#1 — pass physical b_widths instead); kc=4 assumes SS edges; D11 is triangle-local (direction mismatch V#2); foundation model is well-calibrated to converged eigen for the OPERATIONAL envelope but NON-conservative for slam (CLAUDE.md / findings). Constants (0.605, 0.65 knockdown, kc=4) are durable and reusable for the wingmast; the elastic-foundation idea also models the skin laterally restraining the spar.

modules.purpose: Linear eigenvalue buckling: smallest positive λ of K φ = −λ Kσ φ on free DOFs. Dense Cholesky reduction of K to a standard symmetric eigenproblem (scipy.linalg.eigh), returns ascending multipliers + unit-norm modes. LAMBDA_CAP=1e6 → reported as no buckling.
modules.notes: Dense by deliberate choice — sizing meshes are small (medium 16x8 ≈ 800 free DOF) where dense is robust near clustered modes; revisit sparse only at measured need. Sign convention: Kg tension-positive (stabilizing). This is the verification engine for the converged-mesh check CLAUDE.md mandates. Directly reusable. Caller must build K_ff and Kg_ff on the free DOFs.

modules.purpose: 3D Euler-Bernoulli frame FEA: prismatic beam elements, 6 DOF/node, axial + 2-plane bending + St-Venant torsion. BeamSection (circular/annular), local 12x12 stiffness, global solve with full clamps, per-element von-Mises proxy.
modules.notes: Element: 2-node Euler-Bernoulli (no shear deformation, no offset/eccentricity, no consistent-mass). _element_rotation picks the up-vector via a hardcoded |cosθ|>0.99 near-axis test ([0,0,1] else [0,1,0]) — for a near-vertical wingmast spar (axis ≈ +Z) this flips to the [0,1,0] reference, which is fine but worth verifying the local y/z bending planes are what you expect. Assumes Iy==Iz for the bending-force proxy (circular). Reusable as the spar's beam backbone; annular section is ready for a tube spar. AeroSandbox-free.

modules.purpose: Builds geometric (stress) stiffness Kσ from a solved stress state for linear buckling. Beam: consistent Euler-Bernoulli Kg from element axial force (Przemieniecki). Shell tri: membrane-stress Kg on the transverse-w field with CST-style linear w interpolation (Kg=t·A·Gᵀ[σ]G). Assembles global Kσ.
modules.notes: Validated: column refs <0.3% at 8 elements (test_pinned_pinned/cantilever_column_euler_load, rel 2e-3); SS-plate kc=4 ~3% at 12x12 grid (test_ss_plate_uniaxial_compression_kc4, rel 0.05). Documented simplifications: Wagner/torsional-flexural coupling neglected (OK circular); shell uses linear-w (NOT DKT-consistent) interpolation and omits in-plane geometric terms — standard faceted-shell practice but the source of the under-resolution. tri stress is element-LOCAL [σxx,σyy,σxy] from recover_membrane_stress_C. Reusable; pairs with eigen_buckling.

modules.purpose: Tet-mesh the wing OML via build_wing_solid → STEP export → gmsh 3D Delaunay. Returns TetMesh (nodes, tets, surface_tris, oml_tris above aero_z_min, dirichlet_nodes on the spar-base disk).
key_apis: tet_mesh_wing(spec, *, target_element_size, min_element_size, aero_z_min, spar_base_tol) -> TetMesh
modules.notes: Geometry-coupled: depends on geometry.wing.build_wing_solid + WingSpec and the wing frame (chord +X, span +Z, normal +Y). Dirichlet region = nodes within spar_base_tol of the bottom spar-base z (the bearing). For the re-scoped wingmast (airfoil above a transition zone, rotating stock base) the geometry and the BC-region identification both need rework — the bearing supports are now journals at two spanwise stations, not one base disk. gmsh settings (MeshSizeFromCurvature=12, Algorithm3D=Delaunay) are reusable. Refactor the BC-tagging and geometry source.

modules.purpose: Map AeroSandbox per-panel loads (PanelLoads) onto OML triangles as per-tri force vectors in the geometry frame. Bins tris by span fraction, distributes each panel's total over its span band weighted by tri area, applies safety factor + frame rotation aero(span+Y)→geom(span+Z).
modules.notes: Span-resolved only (no chord-resolved pressure) — each panel total spread uniformly-by-area over its span band. Tightly coupled to aero.loads.PanelLoads and the wing frame. The span-binning + area-weighted distribution logic is reusable, but the load source and the aero/geom frame relationship change with the re-scope (a wingmast has a different load definition). Refactor.

durable_knowledge: Element inventory: fea.py = 4-node linear tet (3 DOF/node, isotropic only); shell.py = 3-node flat triangle CST-membrane + DKT-bending + θz drilling penalty (6 DOF/node, accepts full 3x3 CLT A/D); frame.py = 2-node 3D Euler-Bernoulli beam (6 DOF/node). beam_shell.py merges the latter two into one 6-DOF system. No shear-deformable (Mindlin/Timoshenko) elements anywhere.

BOUNDARY CONDITIONS are uniformly full 6-DOF Dirichlet clamps (u=0) on a tagged node set — fea.solve_linear_elastic, shell.solve_shell_elastic, frame.solve_frame, and all beam_shell solvers. In the live model (beams/shell_model.py) fixed_nodes = every form-beam keel-level node, i.e. a fully fixed root. There is NO released-DOF / pinned / spring / journal-bearing BC anywhere in the stack.

Eigen-buckling mesh convergence (findings.md V.3, 2026-06-16): the n=8 sizing-mesh linear-buckling eigen is unconservatively OVERSTIFF (cannot resolve the short-wavelength mode), OVERSHOOTS LOW around n≈12, then settles to a converged cluster floor by n≥24. Verify feasibility on that floor over the lowest 2-3 modes at n_levels≥24 (eigen-only, ~15-40 s/mesh) — NOT at the 16×8 sizing mesh. The 3 g slam-survival 1575.3 kg result was INVALID: its λ=3.77 was an n=8 artifact; converged λ ≤ 1.25 < 1.5.

Closed-form buckling (buckling.py) is well-calibrated to the converged eigen for the OPERATIONAL envelope but NON-CONSERVATIVE for slam (reported feasible at true eigen λ as low as 0.81). Any slam-sized design MUST be eigen-verified at n≥24. The strip-width SS-plate panel check lands within ~10% of converged eigen capacity (conservative) in the aero regime.

Geometric stiffness validation (tests/structural/test_eigen_buckling.py): consistent beam Kg converges to Euler pinned-pinned and cantilever Pcr to <0.3% at 8 elements (rel 2e-3); SS-plate kc=4 to ~3% at a 12×12 grid (rel 0.05). Tension state produces no positive buckling multiplier. Buckling sign convention: K φ = −λ Kσ φ, Kσ tension-positive (stabilizing). λ is the multiplier on the applied load.

eigen_buckling.linear_buckling is intentionally DENSE (Cholesky reduction to standard symmetric eigh) because sizing meshes are small (~800 free DOF at 16×8); dense is more robust than sparse shift-invert near clustered modes. LAMBDA_CAP=1e6.

Composite/CLT path (materials/unidir.py): reduced_stiffness_Q → transformed_Qbar(angle) → laminate_stiffness(f0,f45,f90,thickness) gives A=t·Qeff, smeared D=(t³/12)·Qeff (fractions-only layup does not fix stacking order, hence smeared D). laminate_stiffness_offset rotates the whole layup by offset_deg so a global-datum laminate can be expressed in each element's local frame (off-datum a balanced laminate legitimately gains A16/A26≠0; the shell element handles the full 3x3). tri_element_stiffness_laminate accepts uniform (3,3) or per-triangle (M,3,3) A and D.

shell.py laminate element reduces EXACTLY to the isotropic _element_K when A=t·Dm and D=(t³/12)·Dm (the drilling penalty uses A66 = G·t isotropically). Current foundation+sandwich optimum layup is pure ±45 (0/100/0).

The drilling-rotation (θz) stiffness in the shell element is a non-physical penalty (default drilling_factor=1e-4) added only to keep K positive-definite for non-coplanar facet assemblies. A flat/coplanar patch is artificially soft in θz under this penalty.

Memory: an IPOPT medium-16×8 sizing worker peaks ~18 GiB; safe cap on the 32 GiB machine is n_workers=1. (Sizing-loop FEA assembly itself is python triple-loops over elements — fine at sizing-mesh scale, would need vectorization/sparse-batch for fine meshes.)
Wall-clock measurement is mandatory and estimates run ~10x off; a sizing result counts only if BOTH converged AND feasible; comparisons within ~2-3% are inside the ftol/basin noise floor.
gaps_for_new_spec: ROTATING JOURNAL BOUNDARY CONDITIONS (highest priority): the entire stack only supports full 6-DOF Dirichlet clamps. A free-rotating wingmast on journal bearings at the heel-step and deck-partners needs (a) two spanwise-separated RADIAL supports (restrain the two lateral translations, leave axial and the pivot-axis rotation released or spring-restrained), and (b) the heel-step additionally reacting the vertical/thrust load. This requires per-DOF BC selection (release the pitch-axis θ), and ideally penalty/spring or Lagrange-multiplier supports with finite bearing stiffness/clearance — none of which exist. Today's fixed_nodes = full clamp would massively over-constrain and mis-predict the deflected shape and the buckling boundary (a journal-supported free-rotating spar buckles differently from a root-clamped cantilever).

CO-BOND / CO-CURE INTERFACE MODELING: there are no interface/contact/cohesive elements. Beam and shell DOFs are merged only by sharing global node indices (rigid coincidence); the live model uses 'stiff massless bond pairs' as a kludge for the tube-to-form-beam bond. The skin-to-spar co-bond, the airfoil-to-transition-to-stock joints, and the transition-zone load transfer have no modeled interface stiffness, no peel/shear (ILSS) limit, and no disbond capability.

FILAMENT-WOUND ANISOTROPY MAPPING: CLT (laminate_stiffness) takes 0/±45/90 area fractions, not a continuous helical WIND-ANGLE field that varies along a tapering mandrel. There is no mapping from filament-winding parameters (wind angle vs station, band overlap/thickness build-up at the ends, geodesic vs non-geodesic paths) to the per-triangle Qbar/A/D the shell element consumes. transformed_Qbar + per-tri (M,3,3) A/D in beam_shell give the plumbing, but the geometric winding model that feeds them is absent.

TRANSITION-ZONE / VARIABLE CROSS-SECTION GEOMETRY: mesh.py and projection.py are hardwired to build_wing_solid (uniform NACA-section wing, span +Z, one spar-base disk). The re-scope's airfoil-above-a-transition-to-round-stock geometry, the bearing-station tagging, and the load definition all need new geometry + BC-tagging code.

TRANSVERSE SHEAR / THICK-SECTION EFFECTS: all elements are thin (Euler-Bernoulli beam, Kirchhoff/DKT shell, no transverse shear). A stocky compression-loaded stock or a short transition zone may need shear-deformable (Timoshenko/Mindlin) elements or at least a shear-correction check; not available.

MODAL / DYNAMIC analysis: only static + linear-buckling eigenproblems exist. No mass matrix, no natural-frequency/flutter capability — relevant for a rig that sees dynamic gust/slam and vortex-shedding, and the eigen path currently has no inertial Kg from gravity/rotation either (slam is applied as a static inertial load).

STRESS RECOVERY AT THE BEARING/JOURNAL and at co-bond lines: beam-force recovery assumes circular Iy==Iz and reports only a resultant bending proxy; there is no contact-pressure / bearing-reaction or interface-shear recovery to size the bearings and bonds.

audit.subsystem: materials / composite-mechanics (CLT + per-ply failure for UD carbon/epoxy)
audit.summary: Two-module subsystem under src/wingmast_design/materials/. unidir.py holds the UD-ply property dataclass (UDPly), two named carbon/epoxy materials (T700_EPOXY, T800_EPOXY), plane-stress reduced-stiffness Q, the Qbar rotation, and smeared symmetric-balanced laminate A/D builders parameterized by area fractions f0/f45/f90 (plus an offset_deg variant for off-datum element frames). It also carries P.3 sandwich-core helpers (CoreMaterial/PVC_H80, sandwich D-factor, Hoff face-wrinkling, shear-crimping). failure.py implements ONLY Tsai-Wu (failure index, strength ratio with closed-form quadratic-root solve, FD-validated analytic gradient, and a vectorized per-element batch that gates the 0/+45/-45/90 orientations by fraction and returns the min strength ratio). Tests are solid and physics-anchored (Q symmetry, balanced->no A16/A26, +/-45 maximizes shear, 90deg offset swaps axial; Tsai-Wu R=1 at each uniaxial strength point, shear inverse-scaling, batch==scalar, analytic-grad vs central FD at rtol 1e-6). The code is competently written and well-suited to the re-scope's CLT + Tsai-Wu needs, but it models the laminate as a SMEARED fractions-only stiffness (no explicit stacking sequence, no per-ply z-positions, so true B and per-ply bending stress are absent), and it has ZERO support for filament-winding specifics: no helical/wind-angle layup primitive, no co-bond vs co-cure interface knockdowns, no max-strain criterion, no interlaminar (S13/S23/ILSS) strengths, and no defined cured-ply thickness constant.

modules.purpose: UD CFRP ply property dataclass + named materials (T700/T800 epoxy), plane-stress Q, Qbar rotation, smeared symmetric-balanced laminate A/D/Qeff from 0/+/-45/90 area fractions (and an offset_deg variant); plus P.3 sandwich-core helpers (CoreMaterial/PVC_H80, sandwich D-factor, Hoff wrinkling, shear crimping).
key_apis: CoreMaterial(E_c,G_c,rho), PVC_H80, sandwich_D_factor(t,c), core_ramp(c), wrinkling_stress(E_face,core), crimping_stress(t,c,core)
modules.notes: Smeared fractions-only laminate: no per-ply z-stack so B=0 by construction and D is the smeared t^3/12 model (doc comment is explicit that fractions don't fix stacking order). No cured-ply-thickness constant; thickness is a free continuous arg. isotropic_equivalent_modulus is a legacy beam-smearing path. For filament winding, refactor to add a helical +/-theta layup primitive (currently only 0/+-45/90 discrete orientations are wired into laminate builders and the failure batch).

modules.purpose: Per-ply Tsai-Wu failure in ply material axes: failure index, strength ratio R (closed-form a*R^2+b*R-1=0 root), analytic dR/dsigma, strain->ply-axis transform, and the laminate min-strength-ratio over present orientations including a vectorized (M,) batch used by the sizer constraint.
modules.notes: ONLY Tsai-Wu is implemented; the re-scope's max-strain criterion does not exist. Operates on element-local membrane strain only (no per-ply bending/z, so checks membrane stress at the smeared laminate). F12 hardwired to the -0.5*sqrt(F11*F22) Tsai-Hahn convention. No interlaminar/ILSS check, no fiber-vs-matrix mode distinction (e.g. Hashin/Puck), no co-bond interface failure. Gradient is FD-validated (test rtol 1e-6) per repo convention. Refactor to add max-strain and a helical-orientation path for winding.

durable_knowledge: T700_EPOXY (pultruded, typical, Vf=0.60): E1=135 GPa, E2=8.5 GPa, G12=4.5 GPa, nu12=0.32, Xt=2200 MPa, Xc=1200 MPa, Yt=60 MPa, Yc=200 MPa, S12=80 MPa, rho=1550 kg/m3.
T800_EPOXY (prepreg, typical, Vf=0.60): E1=165 GPa, E2=8.5 GPa, G12=5.0 GPa, nu12=0.32, Xt=2900 MPa, Xc=1500 MPa, Yt=60 MPa, Yc=210 MPa, S12=90 MPa, rho=1580 kg/m3.
Default fiber volume fraction Vf=0.60 (UDPly default). Stated provenance: Hexcel HexPly, Toray T700/T800 prepreg sheets, Soden et al. 1998 — flagged as 'typical, replace with supplier data'.

There is NO cured/nominal ply thickness constant in the code; laminate thickness is a continuous free argument to laminate_stiffness, and orientation content is expressed as area fractions f0/f45/f90 (the +-45 fraction is split equally so balanced laminates have A16=A26=0).
Sandwich core defaults (CoreMaterial / PVC_H80): E_c=80 MPa, G_c=27 MPa, rho=80 kg/m3; core failure checks ramp in over a 1 mm scale (CORE_RAMP_M=1e-3) via core_ramp s(c)=c/(c+1mm).
Tsai-Wu interaction coefficient is hardwired F12 = -0.5*sqrt(F11*F22) (Tsai-Hahn). Strength ratio R solved as positive root of a*R^2+b*R-1=0 with _SAFE_R=1e9 cap for near-zero stress.
Laminate D is the smeared t^3/12*Qeff model (fractions-only layup cannot fix stacking order); coupling matrix B is implicitly zero and there is no per-ply z-position bookkeeping.

'knockdown' across the repo means an isotropic-equivalent-E reduction (UDPly.isotropic_equivalent_modulus 0.5 quasi-iso / 0.85 pultrusion; buckling TUBE_WALL_KNOCKDOWN=0.65 NASA SP-8007). It is NOT a co-bond/co-cure interface knockdown — none of those exist.
gaps_for_new_spec: No helical / wind-angle (+/-theta) layup primitive: laminate builders and the Tsai-Wu batch only enumerate fixed 0/+45/-45/90 orientations. Filament winding needs an arbitrary +-theta band layup (and the failure batch must enumerate the actual winding angles, not just the 4 discrete orientations).
No max-strain failure criterion (re-scope explicitly lists it) — only Tsai-Wu exists. No fiber/matrix-mode-separating criterion (Hashin/Puck) either.

No co-bond vs co-cure interface modeling: no interlaminar strength data (S13/S23/ILSS), no bondline knockdown factor, no separate co-bond strength reduction. The only 'knockdowns' present are isotropic-E and buckling-imperfection knockdowns.
No interlaminar / through-thickness analysis at all: criteria operate on in-plane membrane strain only; no transverse shear stresses, no delamination check, no z-stress recovery.

No defined cured-ply (single-lamina) thickness constant; winding sizing typically counts integer bands of a known band thickness, so a per-ply/band thickness and an integer-ply discretization are missing.

No explicit stacking-sequence / per-ply CLT (B matrix, per-ply bending stress, ply-by-ply through-thickness stress recovery) — current model is smeared fractions only, adequate for membrane sizing but not for layup-order or bending-dominated ply-failure checks.
Material set is two generic typical UD systems (T700/T800) with placeholder strengths; a winding-specific resin/fiber system with as-wound (not prepreg) properties and Vf is not present.
No moisture/temperature (hot-wet) or fatigue knockdowns, and no statistical (A/B-basis) allowables — only a flat safety_factor=2.0 divisor on Xt/Xc.

durable_knowledge: Axis convention: chord +X, span +Z, airfoil normal +Y; pivot/rotation axis at X=0,Y=0. Z=0 is the wing root; transition zone runs z in [-transition_length, 0]; cylindrical spar runs below to z=-(transition_length+spar_length).

Airfoil contour convention everywhere: (N,2) cosine-spaced, traversed upper-TE -> LE -> lower-TE, with a duplicate TE point that the section-face builder drops before closing a periodic Spline. Any Kulfan replacement must preserve this ordering.

build123d loft pattern: build planar Faces (BuildSketch + BuildLine + closed periodic Spline + make_face), place each with Plane(origin=(0,0,z)) * face, add() them in one spanwise direction, then loft(ruled=True). ruled=True is REQUIRED here: BSpline-smooth loft (ruled=False) overshoots wildly when adjacent sections change topology (airfoil->circle morph), producing a bbox several times any section's size.

Transition fairing uses smoothstep blend f(u)=u*u*(3-2u) (zero slope at u=0 and u=1) so the loft meets the constant airfoil above and constant circle below tangentially — OCC could not fillet a slope crease there. u = -z/transition_length.

airfoil<->circle morph is RADIAL and per-point: each airfoil point's angle theta from the pivot is reused for the circle point at constant radius R, then lerp radius by blend. This keeps point density high at high-curvature LE/TE across all blend values, but REQUIRES the section to be star-shaped about the pivot (holds for NACA00xx, pivot_frac ~0.05-0.95).

spar_radius = largest circle inscribed in the root airfoil centered at the pivot = min distance from pivot to surface, floored to the nearest cm for a tidy stock size (~0.08 m for NACA0018, 1 m chord, 25% pivot). spar_diameter = 2*spar_radius.

Taper supports a piecewise-linear knot profile taper_profile = ((z_frac, chord_frac),...) (first knot (0,1), last z_frac=1) for entasis (e.g. ((0,1),(0.8,0.9),(1,0.6))); None falls back to linear root_chord->tip_chord. section_z_fractions places loft sections exactly at the knots so the entasis knee isn't smoothed over.

aerosandbox 4.2.9 is ALREADY a dependency and installed, with the full Kulfan/CST API: KulfanAirfoil class; get_kulfan_coordinates(lower_weights, upper_weights, leading_edge_weight, TE_thickness, n_points_per_side, N1=0.5, N2=1.0); get_kulfan_parameters(coordinates,...) to FIT an existing airfoil to weights. This directly answers notes.md: TE radius/thickness maps to the TE_thickness param; the LE 'tail shape' maps to leading_edge_weight; Kulfan weights are CST basis coefficients (per-side arrays), not literal spline control points, but they are a smooth control-point-like parametrization usable for arbitrary (non-existing) airfoils.

Symmetric-airfoil load-case trick (truss/extract.mirror_family_across_chord_plane): because the section is symmetric across y=0, the (-alpha) load case stress field is exactly the y-reflection of (+alpha), so mirroring already-traced curves replaces re-running FEA at -alpha (4x cheaper). Durable for any symmetric-section analysis.

Voigt stress ordering used project-wide: sigma_xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy (frame_field.voigt_to_tensor). PrincipalFrame sorts eigenvalues DESCENDING (e1=max tension sigma1>0, e3=max compression most-negative sigma3).

WingSpec is embedded in a larger DesignParameters object returned by medium_scenario() (src/wingmast_design/scenario.py); examples access it as P.geometry. Changing WingSpec fields ripples through the scenario and every example, so read scenario.py first.

Provide a fit path (get_kulfan_parameters) to import named airfoils, with NACA-0018 as the reference default. Decide whether the section Spline should be driven directly by Kulfan/CST control points rather than a periodic spline through sampled points (notes.md open question).

Per-station airfoil variation: WingSpec carries a single scalar thickness and one shape for all stations. Need root-airfoil != tip-airfoil support with a spanwise blend (interpolate Kulfan weights along z), analogous to the existing taper_profile knots.

Rotational-center foil offset as an explicit parameter: currently the pivot is pivot_frac along chord and the spar circle is centered exactly at the pivot. audit.summary: Harvested the durable engineering record from a ~157 KB append-only findings.md + 450-line plan.md for a free-rotating CFRP wingsail sized FEA-in-the-loop. The work covers three demo scales (small 5 m, medium 22 m, large 45 m), all NACA 0018 t/c=0.18, taper ~0.6, AR ~6.1-6.25, pivot 25% chord, 16 form beams. The structure is a space-frame of UD-CFRP shell-following form beams wrapped in a load-bearing filament-wound skin (DKT+CST shell). The single most important cross-cutting result: the design is STIFFNESS/BUCKLING-governed and never strength-governed (Tsai-Wu R ~7 vs SF 2). The medium (22 m) operational headline is 1021.6 kg (eigen-verified, -54.5% vs the V.6 2248 kg baseline), driven down by a torsion-spine core tube, hollow form beams, a PVC-H80-class sandwich skin, a beam-on-elastic-foundation buckling model, and a datum_ortho panel check. Slam/survival is the critical open frontier directly relevant to a real sailboat: 3 g lateral slam is a TOPOLOGY problem (cantilever has no chord-normal load path), survivable only with lateral ring bracing (~13-20 mm rings), and the closed-form buckling model is NON-conservative under slam at converged mesh (true converged slam mode is a local inner-mid-span wing-section mode that does not plateau). Two referenced docs (improvement_backlog.md, guided_generative_design.md) are MISSING from the repo. For the Oyster-595 re-scope: plan.md is mostly retire (phase-specific to the demo study), findings.md is keep-as-reference (the physics, material, load, mesh, and lever learnings transfer; the absolute masses do not).
durable_knowledge: MATERIAL — T700/epoxy UD ply (primary, Vf=0.60, rho 1550 kg/m3): E1=135 GPa, E2=8.5 GPa, G12=4.5 GPa, nu12=0.32; strengths Xt=2200, Xc=1200, Yt=60, Yc=200, S12=80 MPa. Isotropic-equivalent beam modulus = 0.5*E1 (knockdown 0.5), nu_iso=0.32, sigma_allow safety factor 2.0. T800/epoxy alt also defined: E1=165 GPa, Xt=2900, Xc=1500 MPa, rho 1580. Core: PVC-H80-class (rho ~80 kg/m3) for sandwich skin.

GOVERNING PHYSICS (the headline finding, robust across every increment) — the structure is STIFFNESS/BUCKLING-governed, NEVER strength-governed. Beam stress ~42 MPa vs 1100 MPa allowable (~26x margin); proper per-ply Tsai-Wu min strength ratio R=7.0 vs required SF 2.0. Strength constraints have never bound at any design point. von-Mises proxy and Tsai-Wu give the same design (30.11 vs 30.07 kg). Tsai-Wu uses F12=-0.5*sqrt(F11*F22), material SF 2.0, first-ply, smeared laminate.

THE LOAD-BEARING SKIN IS THE DOMINANT LEVER. Coupling the skin as a structural shell (replacing ring connectors) cut mass 37% (43.5 -> 27.5 kg on the small wing); skin then becomes ~2/3-3/4 of total mass. The only consistently positive non-topology mass lever afterward is direct skin tailoring (per-band thickness, -8.1%). Beam-LAYOUT levers are dead/marginal while panel buckling governs: F.1 stress-weighted spacing ~-1%, F.2 diagonal lattice +83% (negative), tip gusset +8.3% (negative), mirror-symmetric respacing +2.7% (negative). Even arc-length spacing minimizes the largest panel = what a panel-buckling-governed skin wants.

COHERENT (manufacturable) anisotropy PAYS: a consistent span ply datum (ply angles measured vs span axis, ply_angle_datum) was simultaneously buildable AND 26% lighter (25.6 -> 19.0 kg) than the incoherent per-triangle-local optimum. Physically: longitudinal beams carry spanwise bending, so the skin's efficient role is chordwise/hoop fibres for shear/section-shape. The current (foundation+sandwich) regime optimum layup is pure +/-45 (0/100/0), confirmed coherent. CAVEAT: per-triangle-local layups (pre-datum, ~50/50 spanwise/chordwise triangle frames) are NOT a manufacturable fibre prescription.

AERO LOAD CASES (DESIGN_CASES, sized for a 5 m demo on a small dinghy; a LoadCase = apparent wind speed + trim AoA + altitude + safety/gust factor): nominal_trim 10 m/s @ 8 deg; max_aoa 15 m/s @ 12 deg (near stall); design_gust 15 m/s @ 8 deg with 1.5x gust factor; survival 25 m/s @ 6 deg (dumped AoA); feathered 25 m/s @ 0 deg (passively feathered). These are demo-scale and explicitly meant to be re-tuned per platform.

INERTIAL / BODY LOAD CASES (accel_vectors body loads in the wing frame, z=span; FD-validated lambda^T df/dx adjoint term): self-weight upright + 30 deg heel gravity adds +15.5% mass (2006.3 -> 2316.9 kg on the medium strip baseline) and is the V.6 STANDARD set. 30 deg heel = g*(sin(theta)*y_hat - cos(theta)*z_hat). Slam = a chord-normal lateral inertial case (1 g/2 g/3 g lateral + 1 g vertical), handled as a separate ultimate envelope.

SLAM IS A TOPOLOGY PROBLEM, NOT A SIZING ONE (most strategically important for a real sailboat). A chord-normal inertial (wave-slam) load has NO efficient load path in a pure spanwise-cantilever wing topology: the beams carry spanwise bending and the skin braces them, but nothing carries a large transverse inertial load except added LATERAL bracing. At 3 g lateral the optimizer spent +53% mass and still produced eigen lambda 0.81 < 1 (buckles). Aero+gravity hid this because those loads are predominantly spanwise/chordwise in the beams' strong planes.

RING BRACING MAKES 3 g SLAM SURVIVABLE (lateral transverse ring members, brace_radius DV + elastic-foundation k_ring credit, k_eff = k_skin + k_ring). Post-hoc eigen sweep on the medium braced 3 g design vs ring radius: 2 mm -> lambda 0.77, 10 mm -> 1.10, 12 mm -> 1.42, 14 mm -> 1.91, 20 mm -> 3.16, 50 mm -> 11.7 (these were n=8 values, later shown inflated). So ~13-20 mm rings clear the SF 1.5 gate. Failed slam runs were OPTIMIZER blindness (closed-form non-conservative under slam => optimizer drove rings to the 2 mm floor as pure mass), not physics. Fix: PIN a ring-size floor (~15-20 mm) OR put true eigen in the loop.

3 g SLAM SURVIVAL MASS (medium 22 m): 1575.3 kg, converged, n=8 eigen 3.77 (+54% vs the 1021.6 kg operational headline). Breakdown: beams 568 + core TUBE 666 + skin 163 + core 95 + brace 83 kg. The central core tube RE-TASKS from a ~5 kg torsion spine (operational) to a 666 kg BENDING SPAR carrying the 3 g lateral inertial bending of the cantilever. Slam is BUCKLING-governed not deflection-governed (optimum deflects 1.9% span anyway). BUT this 1575.3 kg rating is INVALID at converged mesh (see next item).

MESH-CONVERGENCE & BUCKLING-VERIFICATION (a hard-won, expensive lesson). SIZING uses a coarse n=8 (16x8) mesh with a calibrated closed-form buckling SF 1.5. The n=8 linear-buckling EIGEN verification is unconservatively overstiff: it overshoots low at n~12 then recovers to a converged cluster FLOOR by n>=24. Protocol: VERIFY buckling at n>=24 (eigen-only, ~15-40 s/mesh) judging the converged cluster floor over the lowest 2-3 modes. For the OPERATIONAL envelope the closed-form is WELL-CALIBRATED (converged eigen ~1.5-1.6 == SF 1.5; the 1021.6 kg headline is VALID). For SLAM the closed-form is NON-conservative.

SLAM CONVERGED MODE (research-open). The governing converged slam buckling mode is a LOCAL inner-mid-span (z~7.7-7.9 m) wing-section mode: 100% of modal translation in wing-section grid nodes, 0% in the tube/rings, ~8-10 of 400-950 nodes participating. It does NOT plateau (lambda1 2.42->1.44->1.12 at n=24/40/56, ~-22%/refine). So even the verification mesh isn't settled for slam, the closed-form foundation model is non-conservative for it, and the true slam survival mass is HEAVIER than 1575.3 kg (unbounded by current data). The fix is stiffening the inner-mid-span wing section, NOT bigger rings/tube.

MASS LEVERS THAT WORKED (medium 22 m, cumulative): V.6 baseline 2248 kg -> core TUBE as torsion spine -8.3% (twist un-binds -50.7->0 kg/deg, skin sheds 180 kg of torsion plies; tube stays minimal ~5-8 kg at the 20 mm bound, centroidal bending is worthless) -> hollow form-beam segments (complementary: spine frees twist, then hollow walls harvest beams; hollow-only is +1.2% = no win) -> PVC-sandwich skin (D-factor phi(t,c)=1/4+3(c/t+1/2)^2; t_core ~4.3 mm + 1.9 mm faces => skin 519+61 kg vs 1246 monolithic, ~-53% skin mass) -> beam-on-elastic-foundation buckling model (Pcr=2*sqrt(k*EI), k=3*D22_chord*(1/wl^3+1/wr^3); -34% step) -> datum_ortho panel check -> multistart 1021.6 kg.

MASS LEVERS THAT FAILED (negatives are findings): tip gusset +8.3% (kills twist 5->0.03 deg but redistributes load in a buckling-governed structure); F.2 diagonal/helix lattice +83% (long compression members forced fat by their own Euler buckling, relieve no binding constraint while buckling governs with twist slack); mirror-symmetric stress-weighted respacing +2.7% (clustering beams enlarges gap panels); centroidal core tube as a bending member (no leverage inside a 0.5-1.9 m deep monocoque - kept only as torsion spine + manufacturing aid); P.2 hoop prestress (NULL at the optimum, lambda 2.443->2.445); IsoTruss spokes variant 3417 kg (hub diaphragms restructure load paths). All layout-lever negatives are AERO-regime; under SLAM lateral bracing flips to binding.

BUCKLING CHECK FORMULAS: beam Euler Pcr=pi^2*EI/(KL)^2 element-length (the skin restrains nodes) - but this is a SUB-ELEMENT mesh artifact superseded by the foundation model. Skin panel plate-buckling: original triangle-as-plate b=sqrt(area), kc=4 SS edges; superseded by strip width-based (b = physical chordwise beam spacing, median 0.449 m) which gave -18.8% (medium 1-band 2471->2006 kg). Final datum_ortho orthotropic long-SS-plate: N_cr=(2*pi^2/b^2)*(sqrt(D11*D22)+D12+2*D66), 1=span 2=chord, reduces to kc=4 for isotropic. Brazier crush M_cr=(2*sqrt(2)/9)*pi*E*r*t^2/sqrt(1-nu^2) - CHECKED on the survival tube (r/t~79 transition): 6.58x margin, NOT governing.

N_BEAMS = 16 is the measured optimum (swept n in {12..28}). n=20 +2.5%, n=24 closed-form-feasible but eigen-rejected. Below 16 => larger chordwise panels => panel buckling (slack at n=16, util 0.71) becomes binding. The original default 16 is now a measured result. A rigorous re-sweep under the current regime is deferred (cold-chain-per-n_beams hits IPOPT restoration stalls); needs a chordwise warm-start. n=16 / 1021.6 kg stands as near-optimal.

SHADOW PRICES (KKT multipliers -> kg/unit, FD-validated 0.02-0.5%): on the 1021.6 kg headline beam buckling is the SOLE binding lever at +1030.8 kg/SF (every other price exactly 0: deflection util 0.57, twist 0.26, panel buckling 0.71, all slack). This ~doubled vs the old V.6 +531 kg/SF - the lighter design is MORE buckling-critical. Twist limit (5 deg, an admitted heuristic) priced -41.3 kg/deg when banding made it bind = the cheapest kg available. The remaining beam-buckling harvest is closed-form CONSERVATISM (SF 1.5 met while true eigen 2.76 = 1.84x), recoverable only by in-loop eigen (V.9) - but that prize is only ~14% (~145 kg) and the true eigen is a CLIFF (a 17% SF cut crashed lambda 2.76->0.83).

SMALL (5 m) WINGSAIL mass progression: Phase-C beams-only 43.5 kg (tip deflection) -> +load-bearing skin 27.5 kg (twist) -> +CLT anisotropic 25.6 kg -> +span ply datum no-buckling 19.0 kg -> fully constrained (datum+buckling SF 1.5) 30.15 kg (beam+panel buckling) -> +4 thickness bands 27.67 kg (-8.1%, twist) -> V.6 re-baseline (strip + gravity/heel + pressure, eigen-verified) 25.13 kg, 4-band, lambda_cr 2.00. GEOMETRY: span 5.0, root chord 1.0, tip chord 0.6, t/c 0.18, pivot 25% chord, spar radius derived 80 mm (max inscribed circle at pivot, floored to cm), shell 3 mm.

OPTIMIZATION HYGIENE / SOLVER LESSONS: SLSQP needs O(1) normalization (raw Pa-vs-metre scales make the QP ill-conditioned and quit early). Local optima abound - FD and analytic gradients landed in basins ~2% apart, so same-config comparisons under ~2-3% are within the basin/ftol noise floor (measured feasible-basin scatter 2.9% at medium scale). max-based constraints have argmax-switching Jacobian KINKS that stall BOTH SLSQP (active-set churn) and IPOPT (C2 break) - the unlock was KS soft-max aggregation (rho~50 on normalized constraints, conservative, re-validate vs hard-max) over both elements AND load cases. IPOPT trigger: SLSQP stalls or DVs > ~150. cyipopt needs the brew/conda Ipopt binary (no macOS arm64 wheel).

MEASURED COMPUTE & MEMORY (the no-estimate convention): a medium SLSQP iteration was ~26 s recorded; the V.0.1 SensCache cache fix (threaded through beam_con_jac) made it 1.13 s/iter = ~23x faster, medium sizing now ~6 min (estimates ran up to ~10x off, hence the measure-never-estimate rule). Analytic adjoint Jacobian + per-element dK caching = 1.98x exact (FEA solve per evaluate x Jacobian width x maxiter dominates, NOT inner Python loops). A medium IPOPT 16x8 worker PEAKS ~17.8 GiB (not the ~9 first estimated) => on a 32 GiB machine the safe cap is n_workers=1; 8-way oversubscription caused two watchdog kernel panics (vm-compressor jetsam storms).

PIPELINE / TOOLING: build123d wing OML solid -> AeroSandbox per-panel pressure -> roll-our-own numpy/scipy linear-tet FEA (Cauchy stress) + DKT+CST shell; form-beam splines on the OML (scipy splprep cubic B-splines through on-surface points, LE+TE+14 arc-spaced); beams sized FEA-in-the-loop, lofted as inward-arc LENS sections (circular fallback unused). FEA system is tiny (768 DOF, splu sub-ms). Mesh: target_element_size 0.05 m; frame-field n_levels 24. Smoothstep easing on the airfoil->circle morph avoids fillets (OCC cannot blend the morphing loft). Geometry built at 60 levels (sizing at 8) cut on-surface error 289->113 mm.

DESIGN/PROCESS CONVENTIONS: a sizing result counts ONLY if converged AND feasible AND eigen-verified at converged mesh; record measured wall-clock + ru_maxrss in every run meta; negative results recorded with equal rigor; warm-start sweeps (each point from the nearest prior optimum, fine meshes from resampled coarse via resample_segment_radii); milestones export CAD (STL/STEP) + FEA fields (VTU); legacy sizers (beams/sizing.py, beams/shell_sizing.py) are FROZEN, new work goes to laminate_sizing.py + sensitivity.py; every new analytic gradient gets an FD-validation test (central diff, rel-err <= ~1e-4). Incumbent guard: optimizer never returns worse than a feasible seed. Reproducibility is ulp-sensitive (a 1-ulp sqrt(area)^2 vs area change flipped a cold-start basin 10%).

research.topic: Structural design loads on an Oyster-595-class wingmast rig derived from righting moment (two free-standing rotating soft-wingsail masts)
research.summary: Standard yacht-rig practice (Nordic Boat Standard / Skene / Principles of Yacht Design, codified in ISO 12215-9 and the Ploe/UniGe scantling thesis) sizes a rig from the boat's righting moment: in steady equilibrium the maximum steady heeling moment the boat can carry equals its maximum righting moment, and the equivalent transverse aerodynamic force is that moment divided by the lever from the sail centre-of-effort (CoE) down to the keel's centre-of-lateral-resistance (CLR). I assumed RM_max = 225 kN.m for the Oyster-595-class boat (mid of the prompt's 150-300 kN.m band; independently bracketed at ~150-225 kN.m from loaded displacement ~38 t x g x GZmax ~0.4-0.6 m, and RM30 ~150-186 kN.m), and an NBS rig-sizing reference RM30 = 175 kN.m. Splitting RM_max 50:50 over two masts gives 112.5 kN.m and an equivalent transverse force of ~8.0 kN per mast over a 14 m heeling lever (CoE 12.5 m above WL + CLR 1.5 m below). As a FREE-STANDING (unstayed) cantilever wingmast, the governing action is base/partners bending: F x (CoE above partners, 10.7 m) = ~86 kN.m per mast, raised to a DESIGN value of ~129 kN.m with the NBS dynamic factor 1.5 (or ~172 kN.m at a slam/impact DAF of 2.0). Because there are no shrouds, the conventional Skene compression (2.78 x RM/half-beam ~91 kN/mast) does NOT apply - the wingmast is bending-driven, not compression-driven. The torsion about the rotating mast axis from an aerodynamically-balanced soft wingsail (pivot near the section aerodynamic centre, ~0.25c) is small: with operational q ~74 Pa, A=90 m2, c=4 m, residual Cm ~ -0.10 plus a ~5% c pivot offset gives ~4.3 kN.m per mast (~6.4 kN.m with DAF 1.5) - roughly 4x smaller than an unbalanced LE-pivot sail (~16 kN.m), which is exactly why the wing is balanced. KEY CAVEATS: all geometry (CoE height, chord, CLR depth, sail-area split) is assumed for an unbuilt twin-wingmast concept, not measured from the boat; RM_max and the CoE lever dominate every downstream number; and the project's own convention (CLAUDE.md) is that these closed-form loads must be FEA/eigen-verified at a converged mesh before any mass claim.

research.topic: Aerodynamics of a NACA-0018 soft wingsail on a rotating wingmast, and sail-area sizing to match the Oyster 595 standard rig upwind
research.summary: NACA-0018 is a 18%-thick symmetric section. At sailing Reynolds numbers (Re ~1e6-5e6) it carries Cl_max ~ 1.05-1.25 with stall at ~16-18 deg AoA, zero-lift/minimum drag Cd0 ~ 0.008-0.012 (2D, free transition), giving a clean 2D L/D well above 50 near peak. Used as a wingsail it is operated far below stall, at the close-hauled operating point alpha ~ 8-10 deg (Cl ~ 0.9-1.1), where the FINITE wing (induced drag at AR~4-6 plus wingmast/skin/seam drag) realistically delivers a whole-rig L/D ~ 8-10 versus ~3-4 for a Bermudan sloop. The "soft wingsail on a wingmast" concept (Omer Wingsail, Wharram wingsail, AWS, classic rotating wingmasts) wraps a fabric/double-skin airfoil around a free-rotating, unstayed mast; the mast can rotate to set camber/angle for each tack and to depower by easing rotation. Aerodynamic balance is set by placing the rotation axis at the section's center of pressure: a symmetric NACA-0018 has its aerodynamic center and (sub-stall) CoP at ~0.25c with near-zero pitching moment Cm_ac~0, so an axis at quarter-chord is nearly self-trimming with low residual torque; distributing sail area fore and aft of the axis (balanced-rig principle) lets the net CoP track the axis so the residual hinge torque stays small. The Oyster 595 standard rig is ~167 m2 (mainsail-furling catalog) / ~180 m2 (upwind, 100% foretriangle). Matching its upwind driving force with the more efficient wing geometry takes roughly 140-150 m2 of total wing area, i.e. ~70-75 m2 per mast for a two-mast (schooner/biplane) arrangement — about 0.8x the soft-rig area, with the gain coming from the wing's higher driving-force coefficient (better L/D) rather than from raw area.

findings.claim: NACA-0018 maximum lift coefficient (Cl_max) at sailing-relevant Reynolds numbers
findings.value: Cl_max ~ 1.05 at Re=0.3e6 and ~1.10 at Re=0.7e6 (Timmer/Delft wind tunnel); rising toward ~1.2-1.25 by Re~1.7e6-4.5e6 (NACA full-scale tunnel). Cl_max increases with Re across this band.
findings.source: Timmer (2008) Two-Dimensional Low-Reynolds Number Wind Tunnel Results for Airfoil NACA 0018 (Delft); NACA Tests of 0009/0012/0018 in the Full-Scale Tunnel (Re 1.7e6-4.5e6 for max lift).

findings.source: Sheldahl & Klimas SAND80-2114 (Re 1e4-1e7 synthesized database); Timmer Delft data; NACA full-scale tunnel (min drag measured Re 1.8e6-7e6).

findings.value: Close-hauled the wing is trimmed to alpha ~ 8-10 deg, Cl ~ 0.9-1.1, deliberately short of the ~16-18 deg stall so it stays attached and high-L/D. Wikipedia: a wingsail close-hauled at ~30 deg apparent runs ~10 deg AoA vs 15-20 deg for conventional jib/main.
findings.source: Wikipedia Wingsail; Forces on sails; Omer Wingsail (maintains 0-10 deg AoA).

findings.claim: Lift-to-drag advantage of a wingsail over a soft sloop rig
findings.value: 2D NACA-0018 L/D peaks well above 50; as a finite rig (induced drag at AR~4-6 + wingmast/skin/seam drag) a realistic whole-rig L/D ~ 8-10, versus ~3-4 for a Bermudan sloop close-hauled. Wingsails give more lift and a better L/D than traditional sails.
findings.source: Wikipedia Wingsail; Marchaj-type sail-aerodynamics conventions; airfoil polar databases (Airfoil Tools / Sheldahl-Klimas).

findings.claim: Soft wingsail on a rotating wingmast — concept
findings.value: An unstayed, free-rotating mast carries a double-skin/fabric airfoil. Rotating the mast sets the section angle and camber and reverses camber for each tack; easing rotation depowers (softens) the rig. Soft wingsails can be reefed/furled/stowed like conventional sails, unlike hard wings.
findings.source: Wikipedia Wingsail; Omer Wingsail (rotating A-frame mast, U-shaped leading edge + two sliding sails); Wharram Wingsail Rig; RCsailing wingmast forum.

findings.claim: Aerodynamic balance about the rotation axis -> residual torque
findings.value: Residual hinge torque = aerodynamic force x (distance from rotation axis to center of pressure). A symmetric NACA-0018 has its aerodynamic center / sub-stall CoP at ~0.25c with Cm_ac ~ 0; putting the rotation axis at the quarter-chord makes the section nearly self-trimming (low residual torque) until stall, when the CoP moves aft. Distributing sail area fore and aft of the axis (balanced-rig principle) keeps the net CoP near the axis so the free-rotating rig weathercocks to a small set AoA with minimal control torque.
findings.source: Wikipedia Forces on sails (CoP/lift-drag decomposition); balanced lug / rotating-rig sources (smalltridesign, RCsailing); standard thin-airfoil aerodynamic-center theory.

Hinge torque T = F_aero * (x_axis - x_CoP). NACA-0018 CoP/aero-center ~0.25c, Cm_ac~0, so x_axis=0.25c gives lever ~0 and T~0 sub-stall; placing area fore/aft of the axis keeps net CoP on the axis as AoA varies. CoP migrates aft past stall, restoring a stabilizing (depowering) moment.
