The one caveat: FoS 3.0 is applied to a survival LOAD (450 kN.m) that I find understated by ~3x. FoS 3.0 x 450 = 1350 kN.m design barely covers the UNFACTORED self-consistent survival load (~1250-1500). So the SFs are fine; the load they multiply is the problem (carries over from c).
checks.corrected_value: All deflection/twist/SF targets are reasonable AS TARGETS -- no correction needed to the numbers themselves. The only action: re-apply FoS 3.0 to the CORRECTED survival load (self-consistent ~1250 kN.m or the locked/parked value), not the understated 450. The framework is sound; the input load must be fixed first.
checks.reasoning: 2% of 22 m = 0.44 m, within marine free-standing-spar norms. FoS 3.0 is independently corroborated by two fields (Sponberg marine practice and wind-turbine gamma_f*gamma_m=3.3-4.0). The interaction risk is that a correct SF on an incorrect (low) load still under-sizes the spar -- so the survival-load fix in (c) is the gating issue.

verify.overall: I independently recomputed all six critical quantities from first principles. Four of the six basis arithmetic chains reproduce EXACTLY (operational base moment 129/180 kN.m, survival q-values 1621/3042 Pa, the slim-strut 426 kN.m, the OP-1 torque 4.29/6.4 kN.m) — the math is clean. Two substantive concerns: (1) MAJOR — the GOVERNING survival case (SURV-1) is internally inconsistent: the basis's own text specifies the full ~3.2 m wing chord (~70 m2 planform) but the adopted 450 kN.m design number silently reverts to a slim 0.7 m research strut (17.5 m2). Self-consistent with the basis's stated wingsail geometry, SURV-1 is ~1250-1500 kN.m, roughly 3x the adopted value, making survival govern by ~10x (not 2.8x) for a free-rotating mast. The single most important open decision is whether the mast can be LOCKED/parked in a hurricane — if so, survival collapses and OP-2 (180 kN.m) governs instead. (2) MODERATE — RM_max=225 kN.m sits at the TOP of the credible bracket (requires the unpublished 38,000 kg design-max displacement AND GZmax 0.60); my central estimate using the published loaded displacement is ~200 kN.m, which scales the operational moments down ~10-13%. Sail-area match (150 m2) is plausible but optimistic for a fat soft wing; deflection/twist/SF targets are all reasonable as targets — but FoS 3.0 must be re-applied to the corrected survival load, not the understated 450. Directionally the basis is correct (survival governs the spar, operational governs deflection); the corrections are to the survival magnitude and the RM_max input optimism, both of which the basis's own open-questions list partially flags.

checks.quantity: (a) Max righting moment RM_max for Oyster-595-class boat
checks.reasoning: RM_max = displacement x g x GZmax. Independently: loaded published disp 33,324 kg x 9.807 x 0.60 = 196 kN.m; design-max 38,000 kg x 0.60 = 224 kN.m; 35,000 x 0.62 = 213 kN.m. The basis 225 kN.m = 38,000 x g x 0.60 reproduces exactly and sits at the top of my independent band. CAVEAT (not arithmetic): this is a DERIVED number — Oyster does not publish the RM curve, and both disp=38,000 (vs published loaded 33,324) and GZmax=0.60 are assumptions. A more central estimate using published loaded disp would give ~195-200 kN.m, so 225 is ~12% high but well within 25%. The basis itself flags this as the single largest sensitivity, which is the right call.

checks.quantity: (b) Per-mast base bending moment, operational, righting-moment-limited (OP-1 50:50 and OP-2 70:30)
checks.independent_value: OP-1: 8.04 kN/mast, 86.0 kN.m static, 129 kN.m design (DAF 1.5). OP-2: 11.25 kN, 120.4 static, 180 kN.m design; single-mast bound 258 kN.m.

Total transverse force = 225/14.0 = 16.07 kN. 50:50 -> 8.04 kN/mast; x arm 10.7 m = 86.0 kN.m static; x DAF 1.5 = 129 kN.m. 70:30 -> 0.70x225/14.0 = 11.25 kN; x10.7 = 120.4; x1.5 = 180.6. Absolute 100%-on-one bound = 225/14.0x10.7x1.5 = 258. Every figure reproduces to 3 sig figs. Method (cap aero force at RM_max, divide by heel lever for force, multiply by partners arm for base moment) is the physically correct way to bound a rig load by hull stability. Minor caveat: heel lever 14.0 m and partners arm 10.7 m inherit the derived CE height; and using RM_MAX (peak GZ at 50-60 deg heel) rather than RM at sailing heel (~20-30 deg) is conservative since a boat is force-limited near upright.
checks.discrepancy: None on arithmetic or method. Loads scale linearly with the derived RM_max and CE geometry.
checks.corrected_value: 129 kN.m (OP-1 design) and 180 kN.m (OP-2 design) confirmed.

checks.quantity: (c) Survival bending moment, bare weathervaned mast, hurricane wind
checks.independent_value: Cat 3 (100 kt), realistic full-wing-chord planform: ~1,250-1,500 kN.m (q=1621 Pa, A=70 m2, arm=11 m, Cl=1.0-1.2). The basis's 426/450 kN.m uses a 17.5 m2 SLIM STRUT that is NOT this rig.

The basis's OWN SURV-1 description specifies the exposed planform as 22 m span x ~3.2 m mean chord = ~70 m2 with arm ~11 m — that gives M = 1621x1.2x70x11 = 1498 kN.m (Cl 1.2) or 1248 kN.m (Cl 1.0). checks.independent_value: Survival (SURV-1) governs the spar strength/buckling; operational (OP-1/OP-2) governs deflection/twist serviceability.
checks.reasoning: Even with the understated 450 kN.m, survival/operational = 450/180 = 2.5x. With the realistic full-chord ~1,300 kN.m, the ratio is ~7x. Either way the conclusion (survival governs structure, operational governs stiffness/serviceability) is correct and robust. The qualitative governing-case logic is sound; only the magnitude of the governing load is wrong (understated). Caveat: this assumes the mast must survive free-rotating; if it is lockable, the governing case can flip to OP-2.

checks.corrected_value: Survival governs (confirmed), but by ~7x not ~2.8x if the mast is free-rotating. Conditional on the lock/park decision.

checks.quantity: (e) Sail area to match standard-rig drive force (150 m2 wing vs 180 m2 sloop)
checks.independent_value: For a PLAIN symmetric NACA-0018 soft wing, ~180-190 m2 (no saving, or slightly more). 150 m2 is achievable only if the wing is effectively CAMBERED/flapped to CL ~1.45+.
checks.reasoning: Drive-force match at equal q: A_wing x Cx_wing = A_std x Cx_sloop. The basis's 150 vs 180 implies the wing's effective drive coefficient is only ~1.2x the sloop's — modest. The problem: a PLAIN symmetric 0018 maxes at CL ~1.1-1.2 attached, essentially the same as a good upwind soft sail (~1.0-1.3). So a plain 0018 gives NO area saving; matching 180 m2 of sloop needs ~188 m2 of plain wing. To reach 150 m2 the wing must run CL ~1.45, which requires camber or a flap — inconsistent with the stated 'symmetric NACA 0018'. A genuinely high-lift cambered/flapped wing (CL ~1.7) would need only ~127 m2. Separately, the operating-q cross-check is consistent: at q~74 Pa, 150 m2 x CL 1.2 = 13.4 kN, near the 16.1 kN needed to reach RM_max, so the rig is correctly RM-limited near its operating CL.
checks.discrepancy: 150 m2 is optimistic for the stated SYMMETRIC 0018 section. The drive-force match implicitly assumes a cambered/high-lift wing (CL ~1.45), contradicting the symmetric-airfoil geometry assumption. Either accept ~180-190 m2 with a plain 0018, or commit to camber/flap to justify 150 m2.
checks.corrected_value: ~180-190 m2 for a plain symmetric 0018 (no saving); 150 m2 only with effective camber/flap (CL ~1.45). Resolve the airfoil-vs-area inconsistency before fixing per-mast area at 75 m2.

checks.independent_value: Tip defl 2% span (0.44 m): tight/conservative serviceability cap, operational-only — sound. Tip twist 5 deg: reasonable. Buckling eigen RF 1.5: standard, low end for ultimate. Strength FoS 2.0 op / 3.0 ultimate: defensible, low end of the 3-4 industry band.
checks.reasoning: 2% tip deflection (0.44 m on 22 m) is a tight serviceability limit (unstayed masts/turbine blades tolerate 3-10%); applying it operational-only and NOT to survival is the correct distinction (matches findings.md V.7). Tip twist 5 deg is reasonable for rotating-wing AoA fidelity. Strength FoS 3.0 ultimate is bracketed independently by Sponberg free-standing-spar practice (3.0 on max RM) and wind-blade gamma_f(1.25-1.35)xgamma_m(2.45-2.94)=3.3-4.0 — two fields converge near 3, so 3.0 is at the LOW end (DNV-ST-0412 Cat I would push 4.5).
